texts: good. the whenever-clause becomes a rule that can actually fire: the trigger is one finite clause whose participants (wind, harbor water, the lantern it happens at) are all ordinary matchable terms, so a later sentence reporting such a reflection sets off the burning. "that lantern" is correctly tied back to the lantern the reflection happened at, and the burning keeps the possessed mire-essence, the "quickly" manner and its simultaneity with the trigger.
